scenes.name: 1 Hook
scenes.text: Two teams studied the same burnt bones from ancient Carthage, and reached conflicting conclusions.

scenes.name: 2 The place
scenes.text: They come from Carthage's [tophet](/tˈəʊfɛt/): a sacred precinct where people buried urns of cremated infants, and young lambs.

scenes.name: 3 Vows in stone
scenes.text: Stones above many urns record vows to the gods [Ba'al](/bˈɑːəl/) [Hammon](/hɑmˈəʊn/) and [Tanit](/tˈɑːniːt/).

scenes.name: 4 The accusers
scenes.text: Greek writers accused Carthage of sacrificing children. None of them was Carthaginian.

scenes.name: 5 Smith et al.
scenes.text: Patricia Smith's team concluded most of the infants died at one to one and a half months: a pattern they read as sacrifice.

scenes.name: 6 Schwartz et al.
scenes.text: Jeffrey Schwartz's team concluded many died before or around birth: consistent, they argue, with natural deaths, though occasional sacrifice may have happened.

scenes.name: 7 Method
scenes.text: The dispute is method: how much fire shrinks bone, and whether it erases a tooth line that forms only after a baby's first week or two.

scenes.name: 8 Open question
scenes.text: One twenty twenty-four expert review still called the evidence uncertain. Offered to the gods, or mourned and buried with care? We still don't know.
